# Sharing

<!-- This file is generated by filen-cli. Do not edit it directly! -->

Your contacts are the accounts you can share files and directories with. To add one, send them
a contact request with `contact-request <email>`; once they accept it, they are listed by
`contacts`.

`contacts` lists your contacts and the contact requests that are still pending, both the ones
sent to you and the ones you sent. `contacts --blocked` lists the accounts you blocked instead.
With `--json`, `contacts` prints an object with the arrays `contacts`, `incomingRequests` and
`outgoingRequests`, and `contacts --blocked` prints an array.

Every other contact command takes the email address of the account it concerns, which it looks
up in the list it acts on (case does not matter), so you never need a UUID; the UUID printed by
`contacts --json` is accepted as well. `contact-accept` and `contact-deny` answer a request sent
to you, `contact-cancel` withdraws one you sent, `contact-remove` removes a contact (after
asking to confirm, which `--yes` answers), and `contact-block` / `contact-unblock` block an
account from sending you requests or lift that block.

> `contacts [OPTIONS]`  
> List your contacts and pending contact requests  
> 🠊 `--blocked` List the accounts you blocked instead

> `contact-request <EMAIL>`  
> Send a contact request  
> 🠊 `<EMAIL>` The email address of the account to send it to

> `contact-accept <REQUEST>`  
> Accept a contact request sent to you  
> 🠊 `<REQUEST>` The email address (or UUID) of the request

> `contact-deny <REQUEST>`  
> Deny a contact request sent to you  
> 🠊 `<REQUEST>` The email address (or UUID) of the request

> `contact-cancel <REQUEST>`  
> Withdraw a contact request you sent  
> 🠊 `<REQUEST>` The email address (or UUID) of the request

> `contact-remove <CONTACT>`  
> Remove a contact (asks to confirm, which --yes answers)  
> 🠊 `<CONTACT>` The email address (or UUID) of the contact

> `contact-block <EMAIL>`  
> Block an account from sending you contact requests  
> 🠊 `<EMAIL>` The email address of the account

> `contact-unblock <BLOCKED>`  
> Lift a block  
> 🠊 `<BLOCKED>` The email address (or UUID) of the blocked account

`share <path> <email>` shares a file or directory of your drive with one of your contacts (see
`contacts`): they can then browse and download it. A directory is shared with everything in
it, and what you later add to it is shared too. Someone who is not a contact yet needs a
contact request first (`contact-request <email>`).

`shared-by-me` lists what you shared, by its path in your drive, each with whom it is shared.
`unshare <path> [email]` stops sharing a file or directory with that contact, or with everyone
it is shared with when no email is given (after asking to confirm, which `--yes` answers).

`shared-with-me` lists what others shared with you, each with who shared it. Given a path, it
lists the directory at that path instead, or shows the file there: the path starts with the
name of a shared item, as `shared-with-me` lists it, and goes down from there (for example
`shared-with-me Photos/2024`). When several people shared items of the same name with you,
`--from <email>` picks the one shared by that account; without a path, `--from` lists only what
that account shared with you. `leave-share <name>` removes an item
someone shared with you from what is shared with you (after asking to confirm, which `--yes`
answers); only they can share it again.

`download-shared <path> [destination]` downloads a file or directory (recursively) from what
is shared with you into a local directory, keeping its name, as `download` does for your own
drive. The path is one `shared-with-me` takes, and so is `--from`. An item whose name is not a
plain file name (one holding a `/`, or `..`) is not downloaded, and inside a directory it is
skipped with what is below it.

With `--json`, the listings are printed as arrays.

> `share <PATH> <EMAIL>`  
> Share a file or directory with a contact  
> 🠊 `<PATH>` File or directory to share  
> 🠊 `<EMAIL>` The email address of the contact to share it with

> `shared-by-me`  
> List what you shared, and with whom

> `unshare <PATH> [EMAIL]`  
> Stop sharing a file or directory (without an email, with everyone, after asking to confirm, which --yes answers)  
> 🠊 `<PATH>` File or directory to stop sharing  
> 🠊 `[EMAIL]` The contact to stop sharing it with (default: everyone it is shared with)

> `shared-with-me [OPTIONS] [PATH]`  
> List what others shared with you, or a directory in it  
> 🠊 `[PATH]` A path in what is shared with you, starting with a shared item's name (default: list the shared items)  
> 🠊 `--from <EMAIL>` Only what this account shared: picks the shared item when several have the path's first name, and without a path lists only its items

> `leave-share [OPTIONS] <NAME>`  
> Remove an item someone shared with you from what is shared with you (asks to confirm, which --yes answers)  
> 🠊 `<NAME>` The shared item's name, as shared-with-me lists it  
> 🠊 `--from <EMAIL>` Pick the item shared by this account, when several have the name

> `download-shared [OPTIONS] <SOURCE> [DESTINATION]`  
> Download a file or directory (recursively) from what others shared with you into a local directory  
> 🠊 `<SOURCE>` A path in what is shared with you, starting with a shared item's name  
> 🠊 `[DESTINATION]` Local destination directory (default: the current local directory)  
> 🠊 `--from <EMAIL>` Pick the shared item shared by this account, when several have the path's first name
